references.text: Moses' staff is first introduced here, the same instrument that Aaron will use to perform the sign
Aaron uses the staff to perform signs before Pharaoh, the same pattern as seen here with the plague of water
The fulfillment of the command given in verse 19, where the water actually turns into blood
A similar command to Aaron to stretch out his hand with the staff over Egypt's waters for the next plague
The psalmist recalls how God turned the rivers and streams into blood so that the Egyptians could not drink
A poetic retelling of how God turned their water into blood and killed the fish
Isaiah prophesies about the drying up of Egypt's waters, including rivers, canals, and pools—the same water sources mentioned here
John's Revelation shows the sea turning to blood, an eschatological echo of the plague in Egypt
In the later plagues, the sea and rivers turn to blood, a direct parallel to Egypt's first plague
A direct continuation of the same plague sequence where the water turns to blood and then frogs.
A theological contrast where the water turns to blood (death) in 7:19, but returns as judgment over the enemy in 14:26.
A direct allusion back to 7:19 confirming the continuity of God's power and Moses' role.
